text:
Mike L: Heads-up — CI rerank suite started showing large NDCG swings after the quantized embed bring-up. Example: master 0.842 -> commit 0.678 on msmarco-hard. Anyone seen label/ordering oddities?
Sara: saw a couple odd CI runs earlier, slightly lower MRR too. thought it was noise. :eyes:
Devon: I pulled the runner logs. Collector merged two qrels files for the same split in one run (checksum mismatch). Might be a race in the qrel collector step.
Eva (ml-evals): I added an assert yesterday to check docid->label mapping; it's failing on a subset: "duplicate docid reported with conflicting labels". Repro looks intermittent.
Mike L: Repro steps I used:
```
# reproduce locally
python -m eval_runner --dataset msmarco-hard --model models/quant-ggml --seed 42 --num-workers 8 --output out.json
python -m rerank_metrics --qrels qrels.tsv --pred out.json --metrics ndcg@10 mrr
```
Devon: Interesting. Two leads: 1) collector writes partial qrels files from parallel workers and we rename/concat without atomic rename. 2) runner tie-breaking uses a non-stable sort across threads so identical scores can reorder. If scores tie, NDCG & MRR can hop depending on doc ordering.
Sara: Quantization increased number of exact-equal cosine scores (low precision), so ties are much more common now -> exacerbates nondeterminism.
Mike L: I dumped an example where two docs have identical score 0.723456 and in one run docA precedes docB, in another run docB precedes docA -> ndcg@10 changed by 0.12.
Eva (ml-evals): Patch idea: ensure collector writes to temp and atomically moves final qrels, and make runner's sort stable and include docid as secondary key. Also add a deterministic tie-break RNG seeded per-run.
Devon: Agreed. Quick patch: replace sort with:
```python
results.sort(key=lambda x: (x.score, x.docid), reverse=True)
```
and in parallel workers set np.random.seed(seed + worker_id). That should remove nondet ordering.
Mike L: I pushed a small fix and a unit test that constructs synthetic ties to the branch: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/482 (WIP). The test asserts ndcg/mrr stable across 10 runs.
Sara: Also adding CI gating: if ndcg delta > 0.02 or mrr delta > 0.01 relative to baseline, fail the job. Will add to the rerank-canary workflow.
Devon: I'll add extra logging in collector to dump qrels checksums and file list to make postmortems easier.
Eva (ml-evals): Added a tiny CLI check in runner to validate qrels docid uniqueness before scoring, erroring out with clear message: "ERROR: duplicate docid with conflicting labels".
ci-bot: Running canary with fix: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/38291 — will report back after 3 runs.
Mike L: Nice. Once ci-bot shows green and the synthetic tie-test passes, we should land. Also update release notes: "Fix nondeterministic rerank metric diffs caused by unstable tie-breaking and collector race when using low-precision embeddings."
Sara: Also capture in docs why ndcg is sensitive to tie order and recommend using tolerance + mrr baseline for regression alerts. I'll add a short note in the eval-harness README.
Devon: Question: do we want to add stable-sort to all runners (retrieval, rerank, embedding-recall)? Probably yes.
Eva (ml-evals): I'll open a follow-up to propagate the deterministic sorting to other runners and add the qrel checksum check in CI pre-step.
Mike L: Thanks everyone. @ci-bot ping when the canary is green. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Canary finished — 3/3 runs consistent; ndcg variance < 0.005, mrr variance < 0.002. Marking build as green.
Mike L: Great, merging and backporting to the quant branch. Closing after rollouts.
Sara: Nice fix — saved us from a noisy flakiness rabbit hole.
Devon: Added a follow-up ticket for postmortem and metric-logging improvements (#2314).
